title: What If Russia Nuked Ukraine? The First 7 Days
description:
Day one, nine twenty in the morning. One Iskander missile leaves a launcher in Russia's Belgorod region, and three minutes later a single 15-kiloton warhead bursts over open farmland in eastern Kharkiv region. This is a day-by-day simulation of what one small nuclear weapon does, ring by ring, and what the first week after it could look like.

This is a simulation. It has not happened. No date is attached, and no unit, place or person in the strike is real. The trigger, the single warhead, the target and the 15-kiloton yield (we found no published yield for Russian tactical warheads) are our choices, not a forecast; the blast and burn figures come from our scenario engine, and we give no death toll because no published study covers this strike. Scenario segments are labelled SIMULATION on screen; facts are labelled REAL DATA or REAL HISTORY.

Chapters
0:00 Cold open
0:39 What Russia really has
1:52 How close it has come
4:39 The trigger
5:38 Minute by minute
7:01 One warhead, ring by ring
8:30 The day after

- Arms Control Association, Russian officials talk nuclear war: https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2022-12/news/russian-officials-talk-nuclear-war-us-intelligence-says
- OSTI, Manhattan Project history, Nagasaki: https://www.osti.gov/opennet/manhattan-project-history/Events/1945/nagasaki.htm
- ANS: IAEA on Zaporizhzhia's fragile power supply: https://www.ans.org/news/article-7086/zaporizhzhia-extremely-fragile-relying-on-single-offsite-power-line-iaea-warns

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the trigger, target, yield and burst type are ours, a scenario, not a forecast. The day-after steps are our assumptions, not predictions. We give no casualty figure for the simulated strike because no published study supports one.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Imagery: NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble; thumbnail backgrounds are AI-generated. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
